newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures ease after Iraq deal confirmation.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures ease after Iraq deal confirmation.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures weakened on Wednesday after the U.N. Security Council voted to approve a six-month renewal of its oil-for-food agreement with Iraq, brokers said.

IPE gas oil futures closed shortly before confirmation of the approval emerged and ended the day $1.25 down at $168.75 a tonne. July Brent stood at $18.81 a barrel at 1454 GMT, down nine cents on the day.
The approval was widely expected and traders said it had already been factored into prices."This latest news has had a small effect, if it has had one at all," one dealer said.
The current deal expires on June 7 and has allowed Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil. The new resolution would renew the arrangement for another 180 days starting at 0401 GMT on June 8.

Prices were volatile on Wednesday but trading volume was relatively lacklustre. "it has been so thin that the market has been hanging on anything that will give them an idea of where it is going," a broker said.
The market earlier appeared to find good technical support, particuarly on July NYMEX crude oil futures, which touched $20.00 a barrel before recovering to $20.15.
